newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CBA FORMS PARTNERSHIP WITH EDS.
newsitem.headline: CBA FORMS PARTNERSHIP WITH EDS.

text.p: Commonwealth Bank of Australia, one of the nation's big four private banks, said on Wednesday that it would form a strategic technology partnership with Electronic Data Systems Corp of the United States.
CBA said that in addition to signing an information technology services agreement with Electronic Data Systems Australia (EDSA), it planned to buy a 35 percent stake in EDSA.
The services agreement was intended to have a life of at least 10 years and include gross revenues over that time of A$5 billion, CBA said.
"The proposed partnership will be one of the world's largest IT (information technology) alliances within the financial services industry," CBA said.

"The major benefits to the bank will be substantial and include cost reductions, improved cost management, ongoing productivity improvements, better application of technology, improved speed to market with new products, reduction of risk, and a share in the revenue from a rapidly growing technology servicing industry in Australia," CBA said.
After including CBA's 1,500 IT employees, EDSA will have nearly 3,000 IT workers in Australia and become the second largest IT services provider in the country, CBA said.
All IT functions, including operations, desktop, communications and applications development are to be included in the proposed partnership.
CBA technology division head John Mulcahy said a small group within the bank would maintain control of the bank's technology strategy.
Mulcahy said in statement the bank would take the necessary time to conclude detailed negotiations.
CBA did not say how much the stake would cost and when the deal would be finalised.

Earlier CBA reported an annual net profit fall of four percent to A$1.078 billion, largely because of an after-tax abnormal cost of A$128 milion linked to an anticipated restructuring of its information technology systems
It also announced a A$650 million share buy-back.
